How often to send invoice reminders

There is no one right schedule, but there is a sensible default. Here it is, with how to adjust it for business customers, homeowners and habitual late payers.

Checked 2026-11-21. Menus in other products change, so a label may differ slightly on your screen.

Short answer: there is no single rule, but a sound default is one reminder a few days before the due date, one on the due date, then follow-ups at about 7 and 14 days late, and a final notice at about 30 days. After that, stop emailing and call. Business customers can get this schedule as written. Homeowners usually need a softer tone and fewer messages.

A default schedule to start from

  1. 3 to 5 days before the due date: a courtesy note with the invoice and the pay link.
  2. On the due date: a short "due today" message.
  3. About 7 days late: a friendly nudge.
  4. About 14 days late: a firmer reminder that asks for a payment date.
  5. About 30 days late: a final notice that says what happens next.

That is five messages over about five weeks. It is a common starting point, not a finding from any study. Change it to fit your customers. Wording for the later steps is in our guide on chasing overdue invoices by email.

How many reminders before collections?

There is no fixed number. A common pattern is three to five reminders, then a phone call, then a decision on whether to stop work, charge a late fee their agreement allows, or hand the account to a collector. What you may do depends on your contract and your state. This is not legal advice.

Business customers on net 30

A company paying on net 30 usually has an accounts payable person and a payment run. Missing the run can mean waiting another cycle, so the reminder before the due date is the most useful one. Send it to the person who pays bills, not only the person who hired you. Ask whether the invoice was approved, because a common place for business invoices to stall.

Homeowners

A homeowner is paying from a personal account, often with no due-date routine, so a plain reminder helps. Use a warmer tone and fewer messages. Offer a pay link that works from a phone. If you send a text, make sure the customer agreed to texts from you.

When to stop emailing and pick up the phone

  • The invoice is about 14 to 21 days late and nobody has replied.
  • An email bounced, or you cannot tell whether anyone reads that address.
  • The amount is large for your business.
  • The customer has replied with an excuse and no date.

Keep the call short and friendly: "I want to make sure the invoice reached you and ask when you expect to pay it." Write down the date they give you and send a one-line email confirming it.

Customers who always pay late

If the same customer is late every time, more reminders will not fix it. Try these instead:

  • Move their reminder before the due date, or send the invoice the day the work is done.
  • Ask what they need to pay on time, such as a purchase order number or a different contact.
  • Ask for a deposit or payment on completion for new jobs.
  • Offer card or bank payment through a pay link.
  • Shorten their terms, if your agreement allows it.

Late fees and their amounts depend on your agreement with the customer and on state law. Only mention a consequence you are willing to carry out.

What the built-in tools do

QuickBooks Online can send reminders on its own. Go to Settings, then Account and settings, then the Sales tab, and choose the edit icon in the Reminders section. Turn on Automatic invoice reminders, then turn on Reminder 1. Each reminder is set as a number of days before or after the due date, up to 90 days either way, and you can add a second and third. Standard QuickBooks Online reminders use one schedule for every customer and cannot leave one customer out. Only QuickBooks Online Advanced can, with workflows. Our guide on stopping reminders for one customer covers the options. Our guide on QuickBooks invoice reminders has the full steps.

Two short templates

Before the due date

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] is due on [due date] Hi [name], A reminder that invoice [invoice number] for [amount] is due on [due date]. A copy is attached. You can pay here: [pay link] Thank you, [your name]

About 7 days late

Subject: Invoice [invoice number] - quick reminder Hi [name], Invoice [invoice number] for [amount] was due on [due date]. I have attached a copy in case it went astray. You can pay here: [pay link] If it is already on its way, thank you, and please ignore this. [your name]

A schedule that follows your rules, with you approving each step

Steadywork can run a reminder schedule like this one and leave you in charge:

  • Follow-up steps send a second and third message after set waits, never early.
  • It skips anyone already emailed recently and flags when someone has written back.
  • A "never write to" list leaves any customer out, such as a customer on a payment plan.
  • Nothing goes out until you approve it, and approved emails go from your own mailbox, with the invoice PDF and a pay link attached.
